record.title: KinDEL: DNA-Encoded Library Dataset for Kinase Inhibitors
record.reason: Include: KinDEL is a drug-discovery dataset and benchmark centered on DNA-encoded chemical-library screening against MAPK14 and DDR1 kinases. It provides replicated target/control count data for an 81-million-compound library, computational docking poses, and smaller resynthesized on-DNA fluorescence-polarization and off-DNA surface-plasmon-resonance affinity-validation sets. The study compares predictive models under random, cluster and disynthon splits. Counts and docking poses are not equivalent to experimentally measured affinities for every compound, and the results do not establish therapeutic efficacy.

record.scope_reason: Include: a purpose-built benchmark and optimization method for constrained biomolecular sequences. Biological feasibility and non-additive motif structure guide the synthetic Ehrlich design; Appendix A.2.7 additionally validates GA ranking agreement on TFBind8, TrpB and DhfR measured lookup data. Main LLOME comparisons remain synthetic and do not demonstrate real-protein improvement. Central independent review agrees; no additional reading credit.

Include: a general graph transformer whose principal real-world application experiments are molecular generation, computational drug-property optimization and eight biophysical/physiological molecular prediction tasks, with molecular scaling studies. Other graph tests are synthetic topology baselines. TDC oracle improvements are not new measured activity, and PPO fails the difficult GSK3beta objective. Central independent review agrees; no additional reading credit.
